feed.title: Russia Plague Watch
feed.subtitle: Independent, sourced tracker of the suspected plague case in Irkutsk, Siberia: live incubation countdown, case counts, WHO risk level, claim check and a dated timeline.

entry.title: WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details
entry.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.
entry.content:
WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.

Sources: CNN, The Washington Times

entry.title: No plague found in contacts tested so far
entry.summary: Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.
entry.content:
Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.

Sources: NBC News, U.S. News

entry.title: Russia tells WHO no plague found in contacts; WHO rates the risk
entry.summary: Russian authorities told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms. WHO's first risk assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. Earlier the same day WHO had said it was still waiting for a formal reply.
entry.content:
Russian authorities told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms. WHO's first risk assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. Earlier the same day WHO had said it was still waiting for a formal reply.

Sources: UN News, NBC News, PBS NewsHour

entry.title: EU monitoring "very closely"; US offers help
entry.summary: The European Commission says it is ready to coordinate a response among member states if needed. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says it is "not cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus". President Trump says the US is "willing to help".
entry.content:
The European Commission says it is ready to coordinate a response among member states if needed. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says it is "not cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus". President Trump says the US is "willing to help".

Sources: Euronews, Newsweek, ABC News

entry.title: Regional commission repeats "unknown aetiology" finding
entry.summary: Officials say the health situation in Irkutsk Oblast is stable. Quarantine measures at the Shelekhov hospital remain in place.
entry.content:
Officials say the health situation in Irkutsk Oblast is stable. Quarantine measures at the Shelekhov hospital remain in place.

Sources: The Moscow Times, CNBC

entry.title: Rospotrebnadzor: "pneumonia of unknown etiology"
entry.summary: The agency says the situation is stable, lab analysis found no pathogen linked to her work, and daily testing of contacts found only 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases.
entry.content:
The agency says the situation is stable, lab analysis found no pathogen linked to her work, and daily testing of contacts found only 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases.

Sources: The Tribune, Euronews

entry.title: WHO in contact with Moscow; White House monitoring
entry.summary: WHO says it is working to verify the event and that risk to the general population appears low. The White House says it is monitoring reports of a suspected case.
entry.content:
WHO says it is working to verify the event and that risk to the general population appears low. The White House says it is monitoring reports of a suspected case.

Sources: CNN, Axios

entry.title: Death confirmed; Shelekhov hospital quarantined
entry.summary: She dies overnight on 1–2 October. Governor Igor Kobzev cites a suspected "particularly dangerous infection". Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova flies in for an emergency commission. 197 contacts are identified and 189 hospitalised for observation. Kobzev says none have symptoms and all tests are negative.

entry.title: Worker hospitalised with severe pneumonia
entry.summary: The 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East is admitted to hospital in Shelekhov.
entry.content:
The 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East is admitted to hospital in Shelekhov.

Sources: The Moscow Times

entry.title: Test tube reportedly broken in the lab
entry.summary: According to media reports, the worker broke a test tube containing Yersinia pestis while handling live samples. Russian officials deny a lab accident.
entry.content:
According to media reports, the worker broke a test tube containing Yersinia pestis while handling live samples. Russian officials deny a lab accident.

Sources: Ynet, CBS News

entry.title: Plague bacterium isolated on the Russia–Mongolia border
entry.summary: Joint Russian and Mongolian teams isolate a Yersinia pestis culture near Sagaan-Uul, confirming high activity in the Sailyugem natural plague focus. Rospotrebnadzor says there is no direct threat to people.
entry.content:
